questions.prompt: How many tool calls should your code expect in one model reply?

options.explanation: Claude, OpenAI and Gemini all document several calls in one reply.
Right. OpenAI says it is best practice to assume there are several.

options.text: One, unless you turn on a parallel setting first
options.explanation: The Claude docs say parallel tool use is on by default, and OpenAI's sample reply has three calls.

questions.prompt: Which pair of calls is better run in sequence than in parallel?

options.explanation: Both are independent and read-only, so running them together is usually safe.

options.text: `search_docs("refunds")` and `search_docs("shipping")` in the same help center
options.explanation: Two independent reads. These are fine to run together.
Right. The Claude docs say tools with side effects, shared state or ordering needs might be better run sequentially.

questions.prompt: How do you limit OpenAI to zero or one tool call per turn?

options.explanation: Right. On Claude, the matching setting is `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` inside `tool_choice`.
`required` means one or more calls, so it does not cap the number.

options.text: Send only one tool definition in the request.
options.explanation: One tool can still be called several times in a turn. OpenAI's sample reply calls `get_weather` twice.
